title: What is Magic?
summary: Two players, 20 life each. Bring your opponent to 0 to win.

checklist.label: I know a normal game is one player against one other player
I know each player starts with 20 life
I know the main way to win
I know two other ways a player can lose

steps.title: Welcome to Magic
steps.body:
Magic: The Gathering is a card game. In this course you'll learn the most common way to play: **one player against one other player**.

Each player brings their own [[deck]] of cards.

You play as a [[planeswalker]]: a powerful wizard. The cards in your deck are your magic. You'll cast them as [[spell|spells]] to summon creatures and make things happen.

visual.altText: Two players facing each other across a table, each with their own deck.

steps.title: Your life total
steps.body:
Each player starts the game with **20 life**. Your [[life-total]] works like health points.

When something deals damage to you, you lose that much life. Some cards let you gain life, too. There's no maximum.

**How to win:** bring your [[opponent|opponent's]] life to **0 or less**. That's how most games end.

check.question: In a one-against-one game, how much life does each player start with?
check.hint: Look at the first sentence of this step. The number is in bold.

steps.title: Good to know: other ways to lose
steps.body:
Running out of life isn't the only way to lose. There are two others:

- **Empty library.** During a game, your deck is called your [[library]]. If you have to draw a card and your library is empty, you lose.
- **Poison.** Some cards give [[poison-counter|poison counters]]. A player with **10 or more** loses.

You won't see these often as a beginner. It's enough to know they exist.

visual.altText: An empty library space, and ten poison counters.

check.question: Your library is empty. When do you lose?

options.text: The next time you have to draw a card

check.hint: An empty library on its own is fine. Think about what happens when you need to take a card from it.
